note: Navigation index distinguishing proposals, assertions, illustrations, disclosures, and secondary statistics. No empirical findings produced here.

claims.statement: The author proposes seven habits for purposeful and responsible work with AI.
qualifications: Not experimentally validated in this article.

claims.statement: The introduction describes four workforce scenarios and favors gradual human-AI collaboration.
qualifications: No scenario probabilities or outcome measurements are supplied.

claims.statement: Pillar 1 recommends active inquiry into AI outputs, assumptions, and limitations.
Pillar 2 recommends changing methods toward lasting purpose, using business and biological analogies.
qualifications: Analogies do not establish causal benefits.

claims.statement: Pillar 3 urges attention to interconnected components, external changes, and long-term consequences.
The author asserts that human strategic and contextual contributions cannot be replicated by AI.
qualifications: Not a demonstrated universal capability boundary; no comparative evaluation is reported.

claims.statement: Pillar 4 recommends defining the desired result before selecting a tool.
The source uses a 60% intake-processing-time reduction in 90 days as an illustrative team target.
qualifications: Not achieved performance, a study finding, or framework validation.

claims.statement: Pillar 5 describes delegation, context provision, checking, and human orchestration in AI collaboration.
qualifications: Teammate is a metaphor and does not transfer human responsibility to software.

claims.statement: Pillar 6 emphasizes verification, transparency, human impact, and long-term stewardship.
qualifications: Broad technical explanations of LLMs are not comparative empirical results.

claims.statement: Pillar 7 combines the other habits to encourage new architectures, governance arrangements, products, and business models.
qualifications: Novelty is not evidence of benefit.

claims.statement: The author uses AI Implementation Engineers / Forward Deploy Engineers as an example of practical human implementation work.

sources.section: Example of a new job and duties

qualifications: Not a standardized occupation definition or measured seven-pillar intervention.

claims.statement: The article repeats an 800% demand increase over January-September, described as nine months 'of this year'.
qualifications: Cites author reflection [10] from 2025; article published February 2026, so year wording is ambiguous.
No dataset, baseline count, geography, role definition, or reproducible calculation in this article.
Not independently endorsed here; not evidence that the framework caused job growth.

claims.statement: Acknowledgment and conflict-of-interest sections both state none.
qualifications: Author/publisher statements, not an independently audited finding.
